# Building qs

qs is a small C library (`libqs`) with two command-line programs built on it: `colstat`, which
prints summary statistics for the columns of a delimited file, and `qcalc`, which evaluates
arithmetic expressions. This document is the build contract. Release engineering checks every
rule below on a clean checkout before a release is tagged.

## 1. Toolchain

- GNU make 4.3 and gcc 12 (C11). No other build system is used.
- `sh`, `awk`, `sed`, `ar` and `install` from the base system. The build finds them through
  `PATH`; it does not use absolute paths for them.
- `CC` can be overridden on the command line (`make CC=...`); every compile and link goes
  through

# qs: the libqs statistics and expression library, colstat and qcalc.
# See docs/BUILDING.md for the targets and the rules the build follows.

.PHONY: all
all:

include mk/config.mk
include mk/gen.mk
include mk/lib.mk
include mk/tools.mk
include mk/check.mk
include mk/install.mk

all: gen lib tools $(PC_FILE)

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)
check.mk
config.mk
gen.mk
install.mk
lib.mk
tools.mk
# make check: unit tests, then the golden cases against the built programs.

UNIT_SRCS   := $(sort $(wildcard tests/unit/*.c))
UNIT_OBJS   := $(UNIT_SRCS:%.c=$(OBJDIR)/%.o)
UNIT_RUNNER := $(BUILD)/tests/unit_runner

$(UNIT_RUNNER): $(UNIT_OBJS) $(LIBQS)
	@mkdir -p $(@D)
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) $(UNIT_OBJS) $(LIBQS) $(LDLIBS) -o $@

$(OBJDIR)/tests/%.o: tests/%.c
	@mkdir -p $(@D)
	$(CC) $(TOOL_CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

.PHONY: check
check: $(UNIT_RUNNER)
	-$(UNIT_RUNNER)
	sh tests/golden.sh $(BINDIR) | tee $(BUILD)/golden.log
# Paths and flags shared by every fragment.

BUILD  := build
OBJDIR := $(BUILD)/obj
LIBDIR := $(BUILD)/lib
BINDIR := $(BUILD)/bin
GENDIR := $(BUILD)/gen

PREFIX ?= /usr/local

CC      = gcc
AR      = ar
ARFLAGS = rcs
INSTALL = install

STD  = -std=c11 -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L
WARN = -Wall -Wextra -Werror

ifeq ($(DEBUG),yes)
OPT = -O0 -g3 -DQS_DEBUG
else
OPT = -O2 -DNDEBUG
endif

CFLAGS = $(STD) $(OPT) $(WARN)

LIB_CPPFLAGS  = -Iinclude -Ilib -I$(GENDIR)
TOOL_CPPFLAGS = -Iinclude

LDLIBS = -lm
# Generated headers.

GEN_OPS := $(GENDIR)/qs/ops.h

.PHONY: gen
gen: $(GEN_OPS)

$(GEN_OPS): src/ops.def build-aux/genops.sh
	@mkdir -p $(@D)
	sh build-aux/genops.sh src/ops.def > $@.tmp
	mv $@.tmp $@
# make install [PREFIX=...] [DESTDIR=...]

PC_FILE := $(BUILD)/qs.pc

$(PC_FILE): qs.pc.in VERSION
	@mkdir -p $(@D)
	sed -e 's|@PREFIX@|$(PREFIX)|g' -e "s|@VERSION@|$$(cat VERSION)|g" qs.pc.in > $@

.PHONY: install
install: all
	$(INSTALL) -d $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/bin $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/lib/pkgconfig
	$(INSTALL) -d $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/include/qs $(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/man/man1
	$(INSTALL) -m 755

    colstat [-d DELIM] [-c COLS] [--max-size N] [--version] [FILE]

Reads a delimited text file from `FILE`, or from standard input when `FILE` is missing or `-`,
and prints summary statistics for its columns.

## Options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-d DELIM` | Field delimiter: one character, or the word `tab`. Without `-d`: `,`. |
| `-c COLS` | Comma-separated column names, in the order to report them. A name may repeat. Without `-c`: every column in header order. |
| `--max-size N` | Refuse inputs larger than `N` bytes. `N` is a decimal number with an optional suffix: `k` or `K` (1024), `m` or `M` (1024 * 1024), `g` or `G` (1024 * 1024 * 1024). |
| `--version` | Print `colstat VERSION` and exit 0. |

Options may appear in any order. An unknown option, a missing option value, a delimiter longer than
one character, or an invalid size is a usage error.

## Input

- Records end at `\n` or `\r\n`. Empty lines are ignored.
- The first record is the header and names the columns. Column names are compared exactly
  (case and blanks count). When a name occurs twice in the header, the first occurrence is used.
- A field that starts with `"` is quoted: it runs to the next `"` that is not doubled, `""`
  stands for one `"`, and delimiters and line breaks inside it are part of the field. Any text
  after the closing quote, up to the next delimiter, is appended to the field.
- A record with fewer fields than the header has empty values in the missing columns; extra
  fields are ignored.
- A value is numeric when, after removing spaces and tabs at both ends, it is an optional sign,
  digits with an optional decimal point (at least one digit before or after the point), and an
  optional exponent (`e` or `E`, optional sign, digits). Anything else (empty values, `NA`,
  `inf`, hexadecimal, decimal commas) is not counted.

## Output

One line per selected column, in the selected order:

    NAME: count=N min=... max=... mean=... median=... p90=... stdev=...

- `count` is the number of numeric values. When it is 0 the line ends after `count=0`.
- `mean` is the sum of the values in input order divided by the count.
- `median` is the middle value of the sorted values, or the mean of the two middle values.
- `p90` is the nearest-rank 90th percentile: the value at rank `ceil(0.9 * count)` in ascending order.
- `stdev` is the sample standard deviation (divisor `count - 1`), summed in input order; 0 when the
  count is below 2.
- Numbers are printed like C `printf("%.*g")` with `QS_STATS_PRECISION` significant digits
  (defined in `include/qs/stats.h`).

## Exit status

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success. |
| 2 | Usage error, an empty input (no header), or a name in `-c` that is not a column. Nothing is printed on standard output. |
| 3 | The input is larger than `--max-size`. Nothing is printed on standard output. |
| 4 | The input cannot be read. |

Error messages go to standard error.
# qcalc

    qcalc [--version] [--ops] [-e EXPR] [FILE]

Evaluates arithmetic expressions.

- With `-e EXPR`, evaluates `EXPR` and prints one line.
- Otherwise reads `FILE` (or standard input when `FILE` is missing or `-`) and evaluates each line.
  A trailing `\r` is removed. Lines that are empty, contain only blanks, or whose first non-blank
  character is `#` are skipped. Every other line prints exactly one output line.
- `--version` prints `qcalc VERSION`; `--ops` prints the operation table the program was built with,
  one operation per line: `name token arity precedence assoc`, in the order of `src/ops.def`.
  Both exit 0 at once.

	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) $(UNIT_OBJS) $(LIBQS) $(LDLIBS) -o $@

$(OBJDIR)/tests/%.o: tests/%.c $(FLAGS_STAMP) | $(GEN_HDRS)
	@mkdir -p $(@D)
	$(CC) $(TOOL_CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -MMD -MP -c $< -o $@

.PHONY: check

	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)/tests
	@rc=0; \
	$(UNIT_RUNNER) > $(BUILD)/tests/unit.log 2>&1 || rc=1; \
	cat $(BUILD)/tests/unit.log; \
	sh tests/golden.sh $(BINDIR) > $(BUILD)/tests/golden.log 2>&1 || rc=1; \
	cat $(BUILD)/tests/golden.log; \
	exit $$rc
EOF

# make install [PREFIX=...] [DESTDIR=...]

MANS    := $(sort $(wildcard man/*.1))
PUBHDRS := $(sort $(wildcard include/qs/*.h))

.PHONY: install
install: all

	$(INSTALL) -m 755 $(BINS) "$(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/bin"
	$(INSTALL) -m 644 $(LIBQS) "$(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/lib"
	$(INSTALL) -m 644 $(PUBHDRS) $(GEN_VERSION) "$(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/include/qs"
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	p=$$(printf '%s' '$(PREFIX)' | sed -e 's/[\\&|]/\\&/g'); \
	v=$$(sed -n '1{s/[[:space:]]//g;p;}' VERSION); \
	sed -e "s|@PREFIX@|$$p|g" -e "s|@VERSION@|$$v|g" qs.pc.in > $(PC_FILE)

	$(INSTALL) -m 644 $(MANS) "$(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)/share/man/man1"
EOF

EOF

assistant.text:
The build now meets `docs/BUILDING.md`. I checked each target from a clean tree, and `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.

**What I checked**
- **Clean builds:** `build/lib/libqs.a`, `build/bin/colstat`, `build/bin/qcalc`, `check`, `install` and `all` each worked as the only target on a clean tree with `make -j16`.
- **`make check`:** 22 unit tests and 34 golden cases pass. It exits non-zero if either suite fails, which I confirmed by breaking one test in each.
- **Incremental builds:** a second `make` does nothing. Touching a source file, a header, `VERSION` or `src/ops.def` rebuilds what depends on it, and `--version` showed the new version after a `VERSION` change.
- **`make DEBUG=1`:** it uses `-DQS_DEBUG`, and `check` passes in that configuration. Switching between debug and release in the same tree rebuilds the objects.
- **`make install PREFIX=/usr DESTDIR=...`:** the staged tree has exactly the files and modes the document lists, with `/usr` in `qs.pc`. I did not test installing into the default `/usr/local` without `DESTDIR`.

**Build fixes**
- I deleted `include/qs/ops.h`. It was a stale hand-copied header that shadowed the generated one and lacked `hypot` and `clamp`.
- Both headers are now generated into `build/gen`. `version.h` was never generated before.
- Tools and tests couldn't find the generated headers, and the link line put libraries before objects. Both are fixed, and the programs now link with `-static`.
- Objects now track their header dependencies, so editing a header triggers the right rebuilds.
- `DEBUG=1` was never recognised, because the old makefile only accepted `DEBUG=yes`.
- `check` previously ignored failures and didn't build the programs. `install` now installs both man pages. `qs.pc` is written at install time, so it records the `PREFIX` you pass to `make install`.

**Source fixes**
- I fixed every warning in release and debug without changing behavior: unused parameters and variables, `%d` used for `size_t`, sign compares, an assignment in a condition, a missing `case`, and a switch fallthrough.
- I made two small behavior changes to match the docs:
  - Prefix `-` now takes its operand from operators that bind strictly tighter than `neg`. Results are unchanged for the current `src/ops.def`.
  - `--max-size` now rejects sizes that overflow instead of silently wrapping.

I left one behavior alone. Without `-c`, a header with a repeated name reports both columns, each by its own position. The doc only says the first occurrence is used when you look a name up.
